title: Bearing Life to Calendar Years
description: Five challenges convert L-10 and L-50 bearing ratings to calendar years for stated duty schedules, showing annual operating hours, the model answer and the learner's answer side by side; Explore mode then varies the rating and schedule and compares the model with FanPedia's published table.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Converting L-10 and L-50 bearing life to calendar years
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the expected calendar life in years of an L-10 or L-50 bearing rating for a stated daily and weekly duty schedule, to within 2% of the model value.
prerequisites: bearing life as a statistical estimate

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts with the annual hours, model answer and learner answer, each new challenge, the end-of-challenge summary and Explore-mode readouts announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; the L-10 and L-50 bars differ by a hatch pattern and a bold label as well as colour; Enter checks and goes to the next challenge; the answer box, buttons, rating selector and sliders are reachable with Tab.

equations: Annual hours = hours per day x days per week x 365/7
rules: Model answers are rounded to 0.1 year
An answer is correct when |answer - model| <= 0.02 x model; two attempts per challenge
Switching between L-10 and L-50 changes the hours and years shown; the underlying L-10 rating is unchanged
Annual hours are never zero because both schedule minimums are 1
assumptions: A year is 365/7 weeks (Chapter 17); FanPedia's published table mixes this with a 52-week year
limitations: Bearing life is a statistical estimate for a population at a stated speed and load; it does not predict when one bearing will fail
Lubrication, contamination, misalignment and temperature can shorten real life well below the rating

sources: Source: FanPedia p. 89 (Bearings: Bearing Life Overview), L-10 and L-50 definitions, L-50 = 5 x L-10, available L-10 ratings and the published year tables, retrieved 2026-10-08
Challenge 5 schedule (12 h/day, 6 days/week) is illustrative

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice with check (commit a number before the result is revealed), then guided exploration
keyQuestions: Why do the same bearings last 4.6 years on one fan and 19.2 years on another?
Why can an L-50 of 200,000 hours and an L-10 of 40,000 hours describe the same bearing?
commonMisconceptions: L-50 is a better or longer-lived bearing than L-10
L-10 hours equal calendar hours regardless of how many hours a day the fan runs
L-10 is the time at which every bearing fails
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown at the end; mastery is 4 of 5 within 2% of the model value on the first attempt.
